note: Verse 3 promises that those who reach the feet of the one who went upon the flower will live long 'above the earth' (நிலமிசை நீடுவாழ்வார்), which Parimelazhagar takes as the world of release. In 1103 a lover asks whether the world of the lotus-eyed one (தாமரைக் கண்ணான் உலகு) is as sweet as sleep on the soft shoulders of the one he loves (இனிதுகொல்). The conflict holds only if நிலமிசை is read with Parimelazhagar as a heavenly world and the lover's question is taken as a real ranking; on Manakkudavar's reading (long life on earth) the two do not meet.
reason: 1103 is a lover's rhetorical இனிதுகொல் about தாமரைக் கண்ணான் உலகு; verse 3 promises நீடுவாழ்வார் to devotees and says nothing about sweetness or about that world. The conflict needs both Parimelazhagar's நிலமிசை as heaven and the lover's hyperbole taken as doctrine, and even then the claims do not address the same thing.
